newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE FIXTURES AT THE WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE FIXTURES AT THE WEEKEND.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the English premier league (kick-off times 1400 GMT Saturday unless stated, league positions in parentheses):
Arsenal (2) v Newcastle United (4)

Arsenal cannot afford to lose. Newcastle have two games in hand and are five points behind as both clubs and Liverpool challenge for the second Champions' League place next season. Defender Tony Adams is Arsenal coach Arsene Wenger's only doubt after he aggravated a leg injury during England's 2-0 win against Georgia.
Newcastle's Alan Shearer, David Batty and Robert Lee came through uninjured, but Belgian defender Philippe Albert (knee) is still out.
Chelsea (7) v Leeds United (10)

Chelsea coach Ruud Gullit is debating whether to rest Italian Gianfranco Zola, who returned from midweek international duty, as his side aim for a European competition place through the league. Gullit signed Uruguayan international Gustavo Poyet on a free transfer from Real Zaragova on Thursday and he will join the club in the summer.
Leeds, without a win in seven, are expected to welcome back injury goalkeeper Nigel Martyn and striker Brian Deane who have recovered from tonsilitis and ankle problems respectively.
Coventry City (17) v. Derby County (11)

Coventry have won eight out of a possible 12 points, but are still battling to avoid relegation. Coach Gordon Strachan's major doubt is influential striker Dion Dublin who is struggling with a knee injury.

Derby coach Jim Smith's Estonian goalkeeper Mart Poom returned from midweek international duty with a dislocated finger and is likely to be replaced by Martin Taylor. Croatian international Igor Stimac is still out with a back injury.
Leicester City (14) v Manchester United (1) (kick-off 1015 GMT)

Coach Alex Ferguson's Manchester United beat Liverpool 3-1 two weeks ago to distance themselves from their rivals and could clinch the premier league title if they win and other results go their way. Welshman Ryan Giggs' could return.
Leicester have secured a place in Europe through their League Cup victory but still have to gain a few points to be assured of premier league safety.
Liverpool (3) v. Tottenham Hotspur (9) (kick-off 1715 GMT)

Anything less than a win for Roy Evans' Liverpool will kill off their faint hopes of the title. The Anfield side will be without suspended striker Robbie Fowler, who leads the premier league goals tally with 31, for their final three games of the season and Stan Collymore is the expected replacement.

Tottenham will hope that goalkeeper Ian Walker has recovered from an achilles injury which forced him out of the England squad this week. Defender John Scales and midfielder Darren Anderton could return after injury while striker Teddy Sheringham returns from scoring on England international duty.
Middlesbrough (19) v Aston Villa (5)

Relegation-battling Middlesbrough face four games leading up to next Sunday's season climax, but Bryan Robson does have a full-strength from which to pick. Internationals Fabrizio Ravanelli, Mikkel Beck and Vladimir Kinder all returned from international duty and Mark Schwarzer will play in goal after recent doubts.
Aston Villa coach Brian Little is likely to bring in midfielder Sasa Curcic if Mark Draper does not recover from a hamstring injury in an otherwise unchanged line-up.
Nottingham Forest (20) v Wimbledon (8)

Nottingham Forest have not won a game in nine outings, but must win to avoid relegation. They will be without player/coach Stuart Pearce who has a calf injury, but defender Colin Cooper returns after a dead leg and Chris Bart-Williams is available after suspension.

Wimbledon's poor run of one win in their last 11 games leaves them with only mathematical hopes of reaching Europe. Midfielder Robbie Earle and defender Dean Blackwell could return after recent abscence through injury.
Southampton (15) v Blackburn Rovers (13)

Southampton will give late fitness tests to midfielders Matt Le Tissier (hamstring) and Jim Magilton (calf) as well as defenders Claus Lundekvam (dislocated shoulder) and Richard Dryden (hamstring). Defender Jason Dodd is suspended as Graeme Souness' side bid to extend a six-match unbeaten run.
Blackburn, still not totally clear of relegation, could be without Scottish midfielder Billy McKinlay who missed Scotland's 2-1 defeat in Sweden with a knee injury.
Sunderland (18) v. Everton (12)

Sunderland coach Peter Reid faces an anxious wait on several players in the run up to this vital survival match for his side. Midfielder Steve Agnew (calf) and strikers Craig Russell (shoulder) and Michael Bridges (achilles) will have late fitness tests and Irishman Niall Quinn is expected to make his first start for the club this season. Caretaker player/manager Dave Watson will be without defenders Craig Short (neck) and David Unsworth (suspended).
West Ham United (16) v. Sheffield Wednesday (6)

This is a game neither team can afford to lose in order to maintain their survival and European hopes respectively. West Ham, boosted by their 1-0 win at Leicester 10 days ago, will be without captain Julian Dicks who underwent a knee operation nine days ago and midfielder Michael Hughes serves the first of a two-match ban.
Injury-hit Sheffield Wednesday will give late fitness tests to strikers Andy Booth and David Hirst., both suffering ankle injuries.
